rows.note: New. A crew is a fan-out of several children under one template with a synthesis step, which cmd.thread.spawn does not model — but it is likely to be IMPLEMENTED as repeated cmd.thread.spawn calls, so the owner should decide whether this is a command or a client-side loop. Payload {thread_id, template_id}. Writes thread-local crew state only.

rows.note: CORRECTED from "new" on the evidence "no cross-thread request family exists". A canonical cmd.thread.request DOES exist, but it means something else: Request Thread, "durably requests a thread and reconciles its stable identity after acknowledgement" — requesting that a thread EXIST. This candidate sends a request TO an existing thread. Two different operations one character apart in dotted form, so this is flagged for the owner to rename rather than quietly reused. Refusals stay typed: refused_cycle and refused_fanout must be distinguishable from a decline.
rows.surfaced_as: More options, Send request to another thread

completeness_gate: node tools/drive.mjs scan fails if any cmd.chat.* id appearing in this workspace’s source is absent from this file. shared/opcard.js stated in its own docblock that "every id minted here is also recorded in candidate-command-delta.json", and nine of its ten ids were not — a contract kept only by the intention of whoever wrote it. It is now kept by the scan. A second sweep cross-checked every candidate against the 540 canonical table rows in Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md and against candidate-wiring-delta.json. It found three rows dispositioned "new" on evidence that was false (cmd.chat.bsd.set, cmd.chat.thread.await, cmd.chat.thread.request) and three ids named in the wiring delta that this file did not carry at all. All six are corrected above.
